intro: Above the Xanthus valley lies Oenoanda, an ancient city in Muğla province whose story runs from the 3rd century BC to the 3rd century AD. It is famous for one remarkable thing: the colossal inscription of the Epicurean Diogenes.
history: Oenoanda was a Lycian city in the north, also known as Termessus Minor. Diogenes of Oenoanda, an Epicurean of the 2nd century AD, had his philosophy inscribed on a vast stone stoa in the city's agora: a lesson in stone for everyone who came to the market.
structure-1: You are now looking at the Diogenes Inscription. In this vast stone inscription in the city's agora, the Epicurean philosopher Diogenes of Oenoanda set out his teaching. Imagine stopping on your way through the market to read a philosopher's words cut in stone.
structure-4: Now look at the towers. These defensive towers strengthened the line of the walls, standing guard over the city.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the Agora, the Theatre and the Walls.
facts: Did you know? Diogenes' 25,000-word inscription is the longest philosophical text to survive from antiquity. The Epicurean had his philosophy carved onto a wall in the city's market, some 80 metres long: the longest known inscription of antiquity. The city lies at 1,400 metres on a wooded ridge, and blocks of that inscription are still being gathered among the ruins.
outro: This brings our tour of Oenoanda to an end. Please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. Some of its words still lie hidden among the ruins; let them rest safely until they are found. Enjoy your visit.
